name: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
aliases: Spirit of Christmas Yet to Come
description: The last and most frightening of Scrooge's spirits: a silent, hooded figure that points to what will be
origin: A Christmas Carol by Charles Dickens
legend: The third spirit comes like a mist along the ground. It's wrapped in a deep black garment that hides everything but one outstretched hand, and it never speaks a word. It shows Scrooge businessmen joking about a dead man's cheap funeral, thieves selling the dead man's bed curtains, and a family relieved that their creditor is gone. Then it leads him to a neglected churchyard and points to a gravestone bearing his own name. Scrooge begs to know whether these are things that will be, or only things that may be, and promises to change.

myths.claim: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come never speaks.
myths.explanation: It answers Scrooge only by pointing. It doesn't say a single word.

myths.claim: Scrooge fears it more than the other spirits.
myths.explanation: He tells it he fears it more than any spectre he has seen.

myths.claim: It shows Scrooge his own grave.
myths.explanation: The vision ends in a churchyard, at a neglected stone with Scrooge's name on it.

myths.claim: The spirit shows Scrooge a future that can't be changed.
myths.explanation: Scrooge asks whether these are shadows of what will be or what may be, and wakes to find there's still time.

quotes.text: Ghost of the Future! I fear you more than any spectre I have seen.
quotes.speaker: Ebenezer Scrooge

quotes.text: Are these the shadows of the things that Will be, or are they shadows of things that May be, only?
quotes.speaker: Ebenezer Scrooge

legacy: The model for many a silent, cloaked figure of doom in later fiction
Every adaptation of A Christmas Carol, from the 1901 silent film onwards
facts: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is the third and last spirit to visit Scrooge
It's shrouded in a deep black garment that hides all but one hand
It never speaks, answering only by pointing
It shows Scrooge strangers reacting coldly to a rich man's death
It leads him to a neglected grave bearing his own name
Scrooge tells it he fears it more than any spectre he has seen
hostIntro: Our final guest doesn't do interviews. Or talking at all. Just watch where it's pointing, viewers.
